dct_description_sm:
The 1991 Census Basic Summary Tabulations (BSTs) are a series of approximately 60 tabulations, each of which features two or more interrelated variables. The tables also deal with a specific characteristic of the Canadian population either as individuals or in their family or household relations, or with a characteristic of Canadian dwellings. All variables covered in the 1991 Census are represented in the BST program. The list of proposed BSTs found below is subject to revisions.

All 1991 Census BSTs are being designed so that the same data are available for standard geographic areas extending from the country as a whole to enumeration areas. Specifically, it is planned that the data be available for each of the following standard geographic areas:

Canada, provinces and territories;

- census divisions and census subdivisions;

- census metropolitan areas and tracted census agglomerations; census tracts;

enumeration areas.

Tabulations on place of work and on internal migration (M9103 to M9105) are the only exception to this geographic coverage approach; these are not available for areas below the census subdivision level.
Most 1991 Basic Summary Tabulations are in ASCII format, with record layouts included with the documentation. Selected tables also include data in Beyond 20/20 format.
